newsitem.title: CHINA: London, Shenzhen bourses mull listing accord - BZW.
newsitem.headline: London, Shenzhen bourses mull listing accord - BZW.

text.p: China's Shenzhen stock exchange and the London bourse are discussing a possible agreement that would permit dual listings, BZW Asia Ltd said on Wednesday.
"Shenzhen is discussing a memorandum of understanding with London," said Huan Guocang, managing director of corporate finance.
The accord would be similar to one previously signed with Shanghai, he told reporters.

The Shenzhen exchange is the smaller of China's two official bourses. It is seeking to carve out a role for itself in China's securities trading after neighbouring Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule on July 1.

Many securities industry executives in China and Hong Kong say that Shenzhen has an uphill battle to ensure its future as an independent entity once the bigger bourse in Hong Kong effectively becomes a domestic stock exchange.
Chinese and British authorities also signed a memorandum of understanding in October of last year on cooperation in securities and futures regulation.

That agreement paved the way for the first listing of a Chinese company in London with the offer of Datang Power 0#0991q.L, which operates coal-fired electric power plants that supply electricity to Beijing and other north China cities. Datang also has shares trading in Hong Kong.
